study: Forecast the next 100 ms of handle movement and area-2 activity
status: New retrospective architecture comparison. September 14 numerical outcomes were previously studied. No hyperparameter or architecture selection uses September 14 in this comparison.

sources.authors: Raeed Chowdhury, Joshua Glaser and Lee Miller

sampling: Existing native-metadata-selected windows for one macaque C. Training uses all September 7 selected workspace-1 originals and held assessment uses September 14 physical blocks 1 and 2, both workspaces. Require finite handle values, finite integer nonnegative counts on selected channels. No exclusions based on movement magnitudes or labels. Data are 10 ms bins. Within a selected original, k = go + 5. Inputs stop at k-1. Reward and absence of another cue during the follow-up are retrospective cohort restrictions.
inputs: Four consecutive five-row tokens [k-20,k). Each includes planar handle position at the end of the block (cm), within-block change in XY from the first to last row (cm; 40 ms), and 37 simultaneous 50-ms electrode spike counts, each summing every available sorted and unclassified column exactly once. The contacts are defined by metadata: sort zero present in all three files. No cell tracking across days. No cue, original ID, workspace, block or target coordinates as features. Train-only featurewise normalization pooled over four history tokens.
outputs: Two separately trained bidirectional tasks. Movement: XY displacement in cm relative to row k-1, read at k+4 and k+9 (50 and 100 ms later). Neural: two successive 50-ms vectors of 37 electrode counts, rows [k,k+5) and [k+5,k+10). Both condition only on [k-20,k); neither task receives outcomes of the other. Target features train-standardized per horizon. Continuous latent count samples converted once to the nearest nonnegative integer in physical count units. No animal-level causal attribution; preprocessing can use later samples upstream.
architecture: Four context tokens projected with separate pose and count encoders plus availability bits, one full-attention encoder and one cross-attending output Transformer decoder. Width 32, 4 heads, feedforward 64, no dropout. Two output position tokens. AR predicts the conditional mean by squared error with shifted true preceding vector and triangular attention during training. Fit diagonal innovation RMS from train teacher-forced full-stream residuals after fitting and draw free-running trajectories at evaluation. Diffusion predicts velocity for both target tokens jointly with unrestricted target self-attention. Hybrid diffuses the current target vector conditioned on clean previous output tokens; train one uniformly sampled horizon per example, using the true earlier token, then draw the first and next tokens successively at evaluation. All decoders use a shared-form projection and fixed sinusoidal time code; no pretrained weights.

optimizer.stream_dropout: 0.6 both, 0.2 only handle, 0.2 only spikes, independently by example; same train indices and modality masks across architectures, and no artificial test noise in full-stream condition.

generative.schedule: 8 cosine signal/noise steps, including exact pure Gaussian terminal noise. v = cos(theta)*epsilon - sin(theta)*target. Uniform positive step at training. Deterministic DDIM rotation per step at inference with fresh terminal normal noise per trajectory. Hybrid draws fresh terminal noise for its next token.
generative.seed: Fixed common inference RNG by model seed and block, reset across modality conditions.

comparators: Train-only horizon mean, persistence (zero displacement, repeat previous 50-ms count vector), last 50-ms constant velocity for movement, ridge on flattened normalized full input with alpha=10, an unpenalized intercept, and continuous nonnegative expected counts for ridge. Each learned architecture also evaluated with handle only, counts only and wrong auxiliary stream (most recent earlier different original, same physical block, workspace and go ordinal; omit unmatched windows only from that paired contrast). Same architecture weights for masked controls; dropout supports each condition.
metrics: Use mean of 16 drawn physical trajectories per seed. Primary movement loss is mean Euclidean endpoint error over two horizons (cm). Neural primary loss is MSE per contact per 50 ms, averaged over contacts and horizons; also report root MSE. Marginal fair empirical CRPS and inclusive central 80% empirical interval coverage with width and finite-sample limitation. Stratify by physical block/workspace. Average windows within original (block + workspace + original), then originals equally, then seeds equally. Baselines evaluated on same rows. 2000 fixed-seed stratified paired original-cluster bootstrap contrasts, conditioning on one held day and these seeds; no multiple inference correction, no cohort-wide generalization. A unique winner requires lower primary error than both alternatives and every prespecified deterministic baseline with the 95% paired interval entirely below zero in both directions. Otherwise report no bidirectional winner. No test tuning; separate train optimizer-update budget from FLOPs, diffusion cost, batch inference and hardware contention.
